investigations.expectation: Noise/arid source lines must be classified as arid and therefore yield no mutation candidates. In particular, a logging call such as `logging.info("x=%s", x)` on line 3 must make `is_arid(...) is True` and `mutants_for_line(...) == []`; instead it is currently non-arid and produces a statement-to-`pass` mutant.

Schemata compilation must preserve the exact number of source lines and leave every unchosen line textually unchanged. With no switch active, `bulk_discount(100)` must return 5; activating the chosen mutant for `if qty > 100` must execute the equivalent boundary mutant and return 15; activating the statement mutant for `pct = bulk_discount(qty)` must remove that assignment and make `order_total(10, 1)` raise `NameError`. Instead the boundary switch remains behaviorally original and returns 5.

res.why: The function correctly reconstructs mutants by adding switch conditions, so it should preserve behavior, and the logic does not indicate any apparent issues that would lead to the failing test.
The function does not correctly handle the switching logic for the boundary mutant, resulting in the original behavior being preserved when it should have activated the mutated line.
The function does not seem to handle the condition for the boundary switch properly, as it returns the original logic instead of the mutant when expected.
